newsitem.title: USA: UAL considers possible bid for US Airways Shuttle.
newsitem.headline: UAL considers possible bid for US Airways Shuttle.

text.p: UAL Corp, parent of United Airlines, said Monday it is considering making a bid to buy the US Airways Shuttle but has not yet reached a decision.
"We've been investigating the possibility of acquiring the US Airways Shuttle for more than a year," UAL spokesman Tony Molinaro said.
"However, we have not yet determined whether or not we will make a bid," Molinaro added.
He said that UAL has spoken with its banks, as well as unions at both United and US Airways about a possible purchase.

The US Airways Shuttle is the successor to the former Trump Shuttle. The commuter service was taken over in April 1992 by a group of lenders. US Airways Group Inc operates the shuttle under a management contract and holds 47 percent of the equity.
In late May, US Airways Group said it has "exclusive contract rights" to purchase US Airways Shuttle and is working with the banks that now own the commuter air service to determine how to proceed.
AMR Corp, which owns American Airlines, has also said it signed a binding agreement to buy the shuttle for an undisclosed price.
UAL currently operates the Shuttle by United, which operates short-distance domestic flights primarily on the West Coast.
